AIRcoin -- Product Requirements Document

AIRcoin -- Product Requirements Document

 Oct 10, 2026 � @omkar

1. Overview

AIRcoin pays people for growing pollution-absorbing plants. A low-cost camera "miner"
watches up to 20 tagged plants and estimates the pollution they remove. It mints AIRcoin
as proof of that useful work. Polluting companies must buy and burn AIRcoin to meet
compliance, which creates demand.

Problem. Urban air pollution (PM2.5, PM10, NO, SO, CO, VOCs, CO) has no direct,
verifiable incentive for citizens to fight it. Carbon credits target large projects and are
hard for households to join.

Product in one line. A plant-monitoring miner, a token minted from verified plant work,
and a marketplace where citizens sell the token and polluters buy and burn it.

Hackathon goal. Show a working end-to-end system on stage:

    A physical 20-plant rig with a real camera, Raspberry Pi and GPS.
    A live digital twin: camera feed with detections, a 3D model of the miner's insides,
    sensor gauges and a minting ticker.
    Live anti-cheat: removing a plant, adding a fake plant or reusing a sticker is caught on
    screen.
    Real miner software fed by simulated sensor data, minting real AIRcoin on a blockchain
    testnet.
    A wallet and marketplace where an owner sells AIRcoin and a company buys and burns
    it for compliance.

Users.

User                                       What they do
Miner owner (citizen, housing society,
school)                                    Buys the miner, plants and tags up to 20
Polluting company / factory                plants, earns and sells AIRcoin

Regulator (government / pollution control  Buys AIRcoin and burns it to meet a
board)                                     compliance obligation

                                           Sets obligations, registers miners, audits
                                           mints and burns

 AIRcoin -- Product Requirements Document  What they do

  AIRcoin operator (our team)             marketplace

2. Real-world system concept

This is the full product we pitch. Section 3 says which parts the hackathon builds for real.

2.2 The stickers

Each miner ships with 20 printed fiducial stickers (ArUco or AprilTag markers). Every
sticker ID is registered to exactly one miner at sale time. A sticker seen by a different
miner, or by its own miner at a new location, is rejected. This stops owners from moving
the same plants between miners to mint twice.

2.3 The 20 prescribed plants

The owner plants up to 20 species from a fixed list. Together they cover every major
pollutant group: VOCs (benzene, formaldehyde, TCE, xylene), particulates, roadside
gases (NO, SO) and CO. The list mixes indoor plants with the strongest lab evidence for

Shreyas turns the evidence into a multiplier per species and pollutant group (High 1.5,
Medium 1.0, Low 0.5) on Day 1. The estimator applies these multipliers to generic base
rates for PM deposition, CO uptake and VOC removal.

Pitch caveat: sealed-chamber results do not scale to real rooms. Cummings and Waring
(2019) estimate 100 to 1,000 plants per m� of floor would be needed to match normal
ventilation. AIRcoin therefore credits estimated removal per plant. It does not claim a pot
cleans a room, and the enclosure calibration exists to replace literature numbers with
measured ones.

2.4 Calibration

We estimate each species' uptake by placing it in a closed enclosure with known pollutant
levels and measuring the drop over time, per unit of leaf area. The result is a coefficient
table: species � pollutant  grams removed per m� of leaf per hour at a reference
concentration. For the hackathon this table is seeded from published literature and
labelled as an estimate.

2.5 Proof of Useful Work (minting)

1. The miner watches its plants continuously and identifies each tagged plant, its
    species, its visible leaf area and whether it is alive.

2. It reads ambient air quality (local sensors plus GPS-based AQI).
3. Every epoch it estimates pollution removed per plant using the calibration table.
4. It signs an attestation: miner ID, epoch, plant states, sensor summary, GPS, image

    hashes and the claimed amount.
5. A validator checks the signature, the sticker bindings, location and plausibility, then

    mints AIRcoin to the owner's wallet.

                                                                                                    Page 4 of 21
 AIRcoin -- Product Requirements Document

Estimation model (per plant i, per pollutant p, per epoch):

  R_{i,p} = k_{s(i),p} \times A_i \times H_i \times f\left(\frac{C_p}
  {C_{p,\mathrm{ref}}}\right) \times \Delta t

k = calibrated coefficient for species s, A = estimated leaf area, H = health/liveness score
(0 to 1), C = ambient concentration, f = a capped concentration factor, t = epoch length.
Pollutant amounts are weighted into one unit, defined in 2.6.

2.6 What 1 AIR means

1 AIR = the health damage avoided by removing 1 mg of PM2.5 (1 mg PM2.5-equivalent).
Other pollutants convert by their damage cost relative to PM2.5, using the central EU
values in CE Delft's Environmental Prices Handbook (Table 1, 2015 per kg).

Pollutant                                 Damage cost (/kg)  Weight (PM2.5 = 1)
PM2.5                                     38.7               1.00
PM10                                      26.6               0.69
NO (NO)                                   14.8               0.38
SO                                        11.5               0.30
VOCs (benzene, formaldehyde and others)   1.15               0.030
CO                                        0.057              0.0015
CO                                        0.0526             0.0014

  \mathrm{AIR}_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \sum_{p} w_p \times \sum_{i} R_{i,p}\,
  [\mathrm{mg}]

Why this unit: it rewards the pollutants that harm health most, it puts CO and toxic gases
on one scale, and milligrams give readable numbers on screen. A full 20-plant miner
should earn on the order of tens of AIR per day, mostly from CO uptake and dust capture;
Shreyas confirms the figure from the calibration table on Day 1. The EU prices are a stand-
in; India-specific damage costs can replace them later without changing the unit.

2.7 Marketplace and demand

    Citizens apply on the platform to buy a miner. A government admin reviews and
    approves each application; approval registers the miner and its 20 stickers on-chain.
    Owners sell AIRcoin on our marketplace for rupee-pegged test stablecoin.

                                                             Page 5 of 21
 AIRcoin -- Product Requirements Document

The regulator assigns each polluting company a yearly AIRcoin burn obligation.
Because factories emit tonnes and plants remove milligrams, the obligation is a set
share of each company's weighted emissions, not a full offset.

Companies buy AIRcoin and burn it through a compliance function that records which
obligation it meets.

Burning permanently removes supply, so steady obligations create steady demand.

The government admin monitors the whole platform: every miner's live sensors and
status, mints, trades, burns and flagged proofs. The government can later run the
validator and registry itself.

4. System architecture and interface contracts

The three workstreams meet only at four frozen interfaces (C1 to C4), so each person can
build and test against mocks without waiting for the others.

5. Global phase scope

The project runs in three phases; nobody starts the next phase until the whole team
passes the gate. We have three days: Phase 1 is Day 1, Phase 2 is Day 2, Phase 3 is Day 3.
Gate 1 closes on Day 1 night, Gate 2 on Day 2 evening, and code freezes at Day 3 midday so
the afternoon is for rehearsals. Epochs are 60 s in real time (time acceleration factor 1).

Global roadmap � 3 phases � 3 workstreams, 3 gates

Each cell is that person's headline for the phase; sections 7 to 9 give the full scope.

Phase 1 � Day 1 � Foundations (build alone, against mocks)

Goal: every component works on its own, with fake inputs shaped exactly like the real
interfaces.

    and agreed on day 1.
    Each person ships a mock emitter for the interface they produce.
    Hardware rig assembled; camera, GPS and Pi working.
    Smart contracts deployed to a local chain; miner software runs on a laptop.

7. Workstream A � Vision and digital twin (Omkar)

Mission: make the miner see. Detect every tagged plant, prove it is the right species and
alive, and show all of it live in a digital twin judges can explore.

                                                                                                Page 11 of 21
 AIRcoin -- Product Requirements Document

Stack: Raspberry Pi 4/5, Pi Camera Module 3 NoIR Wide with a blue gel filter, Python,
OpenCV ( cv2.aruco ), a pretrained MobileNetV3 for plant-match embeddings (no
training), React + Vite, react-three-fiber (Three.js), Blender  glTF, Leaflet for the map,
MQTT over WebSockets.

7.1 Components

 1. Physical rig. A board with 20 pot slots in a 4 � 5 grid, camera on a fixed mount 1 to 1.5 m
    away so all 20 stickers are readable in one frame. One plastic plant and one spare
    sticker kept aside for the anti-cheat demo.

 2. Stickers. ArUco markers (4�4 or 5�5 dictionary), IDs 0-19 for this miner, printed 4-5
    cm on waterproof labels and fixed to a stake at the plant's base. Known marker size
    doubles as a scale reference for measuring plant size.

 3. Tag detection. Detect and decode all markers each frame; match IDs against the
    miner's registered sticker set. Unknown IDs are flagged.

 4. Plant match. At setup, photograph each tagged plant and store a feature vector from a
    pretrained network. Each cycle, compare the live crop above the tag with that stored
    vector; a low match means the plant was swapped and is flagged. This replaces a 20-
    species classifier, which can't be trained well in three days.

 5. Plant size. Segment green pixels in the crop (HSV threshold or excess-green index),
    convert to cm� using the marker's known size. Smooth over time.

 6. Liveness (fake-plant check). Primary: NDVI from the NoIR camera with a blue filter
    (living leaves reflect near-infrared; plastic does not). Fallback: a low plant-match score
    plus texture and colour variance. Output alive_score 0-1.

 7. Status machine. Per tag: present  missing after 10 s unseen  removed after 60 s;
    suspect when species mismatches or alive_score is low. Debounced so a hand
    passing in front doesn't trigger alerts.

 8. Live feed. Annotated stream (boxes, tag IDs, species, status colour) at about 15 fps,
    720p, via MJPEG or WebRTC. The NoIR camera shows false colours, so the twin offers
    two views: the raw feed and an NDVI heat map where living leaves glow. Inference runs
    at 1-2 Hz.

 9. Digital twin web app.
        3D miner model built in Blender: case, Raspberry Pi, camera, GPS module, sensor
        boards, wiring. Exploded view on click; each part shows its live reading.
        Virtual 20-slot plant grid mirroring the rig: green = healthy, grey = missing, red =
        suspect.
        Live camera panel, sensor gauges and AQI chart (from C2), mint ticker and wallet
        balance (from C4), anti-cheat event log, GPS pin on a map.

 AIRcoin -- Product Requirements Document

7.2 Phase scopes

Phase 1 � Foundations
    Assemble rig, mount camera, confirm Pi, camera and GPS work.
    Print stickers; tag detection working on still frames and live video.
    Enrolment script: photo and feature vector saved per tag.
    Twin app skeleton: layout, 3D model v1 loaded, panels wired to the C2 and C4 mocks.
    Ship a C1 mock emitter (replays a recorded scene, can simulate a removed or fake
    plant).
    20 of 20 stickers detected at the rig distance in normal room light
    3D miner model renders in the browser and rotates smoothly
    Twin shows mock sensor and mint data updating every second

Phase 2 � Integration
    Plant-match check, leaf-area estimation and NDVI liveness score.
    Publish real C1 messages from the Pi to the broker.
    Twin switches from mocks to real C2 and C4; live annotated feed embedded.
    Swapped plant flagged in at least 4 of 5 tries
    Removed plant shown as missing on the twin within 10 s
    Vision runs at 1 Hz or faster on the Pi (or on a laptop as declared fallback)
    Twin's coin ticker moves when C mints for this miner

Phase 3 � Demo hardening
    Tune fake-plant detection with the plastic plant under demo lighting.
    Anti-cheat alerts rendered clearly: banner, slot turns red, log entry, mint rate drop.
    Exploded-view animation, polish, dark mode for projectors.
    Fallbacks: vision on a laptop with a USB camera; recorded feed if the camera fails.
    Fake plant flagged in at least 4 of 5 tries
    Twin runs 15 minutes with no reload

Owns in the demo: steps 1-5 of the demo script (rig, twin, detection, removal, fake plant).

8. Workstream B � Miner core and PoUW engine (Shreyas)

Mission: turn what the miner sees and senses into a trustworthy, signed claim of pollution
removed. This is the "useful work" in Proof of Useful Work.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Page 13 of 21
  AIRcoin -- Product Requirements Document

Stack: Python 3.11 asyncio daemon on Raspberry Pi OS, Mosquitto MQTT broker, gpsd /
pynmea2 for GPS, eth-account or coincurve for secp256k1 signing, SQLite for the local
log, systemd for auto-start, a small FastAPI panel for the scenario controller.

8.1 Components

 1. Sensor layer. One driver interface per sensor (PM, gas/VOC, CO, NO,
     temp/humidity). All air sensors are simulated for the hackathon; only the camera and
     GPS are real. Real PMS5003, MQ-135, SCD40 and BME280 drivers can drop in later
     without other code changing. Optional: if a DHT22 or BME280 is already on hand, wire
     it so one reading in the twin is live.

 2. Sensor simulator. Daily curves plus noise, with correlated values (PM10 tracks PM2.5,
     humidity affects PM). Named scenarios: clean morning (AQI about 50), rush hour
     (about 180), festival smog (about 400), rain washout. Switchable live.

 3. GPS service. Reads the real GPS module; falls back to a fixed demo location indoors
     where there's no fix. Reports location and fix quality.

 4. Vision subscriber. Consumes C1 and keeps the latest state of each of the 20 plants.
 5. Species catalogue and calibration table. 20 species � pollutants coefficient table,

     seeded from published studies, versioned; its hash goes into every attestation. The
     species list is fixed in 2.3; B sets the multipliers.
 6. Estimation engine. Applies the model in section 2.5 per plant per epoch. Caps per
     plant and per epoch. Missing plants count zero; suspect plants count zero and raise a
     flag.
 7. Epoch manager. Epoch = 60 s in real time for the demo (no time acceleration), 1 hour in
     production.
 8. Attestation signer. Builds the C3 payload, hashes the evidence (frame hashes + sensor
     readings + plant states + GPS), signs with the device key. Keys generated on first boot
     and registered with C's registry.
 9. Uplink. Posts C3 with retry and an offline queue so no epoch is lost if Wi-Fi drops.
10. Telemetry. Publishes C2 every second and every epoch.
11. Device-side anti-cheat flags. Unknown sticker, species mismatch, low liveness, GPS
     more than 50 m from the registered spot, frozen camera (identical frame hashes), too
     many plants appearing at once, clock drift.
12. Scenario controller. A web panel for the demo: change AQI scenario, simulate moving
     the miner, reset.
13. Calibration protocol (document). How the real enclosure test would work: sealed box,
     reference sensor, controlled pollutant source, decay measured with and without each
     species, coefficients fitted per m� of leaf. Used in the pitch to answer "how do you
     know?"

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Page 14 of 21
 AIRcoin -- Product Requirements Document

8.2 Phase scopes

Phase 1 � Foundations
    Write C1, C2, C3 schemas with A and C; publish mock C2 and mock C3 emitters.
    Sensor simulator with at least three scenarios.
    Estimator and epoch manager running on a laptop against the C1 mock.
    Key generation and signing; signature verified by a test script.
    Draft list of 20 species and coefficient table v0 with sources.
    One command produces a valid signed attestation from mock inputs
    Changing the scenario changes the estimate in the expected direction
    Tampering with any field makes the signature check fail

Phase 2 � Integration
    Daemon runs on the Pi as a systemd service; real GPS read.
    Consumes live C1 from A; posts live C3 to C's validator; serves live C2 to the twin.
    Calibration table v1 frozen and documented.
    Live epochs every 60 s with no manual step for 30 minutes
    Unplugging Wi-Fi for 2 minutes loses no epochs (queued and sent later)
    Removing a plant lowers the next epoch's estimate by that plant's share

Phase 3 � Demo hardening
    All device-side anti-cheat flags working and visible in C2.
    Scenario controller panel used in rehearsals.
    Two-hour soak test on the Pi; watch CPU temperature and memory.
    Calibration protocol written up as a one-pager for judges.
    Each anti-cheat flag reproduced on demand
    Soak test finishes with no crash and no missed epoch

Owns in the demo: step 3 (AQI spike raises the mint rate) and the "how we calculate"
explanation.

9. Workstream C � Token, wallet and marketplace (Umashankar)

Mission: make AIRcoin a real token on a blockchain: minted only from verified proofs, held
in a wallet, traded on a market, and burned by polluters for compliance.

9.2 Off-chain services and apps

1. Validator / mint oracle. Receives C3, then checks: signature matches the registered
    device; miner is active; every sticker belongs to this miner and wasn't claimed by
    another miner in the same window (the cross-miner duplicate check); GPS inside the
    registered geofence; amount within the plausibility cap for those species and that AQI;
    epoch not already minted. Passes  sends mintForEpoch ; fails  stores the rejection
    reason.

2. Indexer + C4 API. Listens to contract events; serves balances, mint history, trades and
    burns over REST and WebSocket.

3. One web platform, three logins. Citizen / miner owner, company, and government
    admin, each with its own pages. Demo accounts come with built-in wallets so judges
    need no MetaMask; MetaMask also works.

10. Demo script, success metrics, risks and decisions

10.1 Demo script (about 10 minutes)

 1. The miner. Show the physical rig, then the twin's 3D model; explode it to show camera,
    Pi, GPS and sensors. (Omkar)

 2. It sees. Live feed detects all 20 stickers; twin grid turns green; switch to the NDVI view
    where living leaves glow. (Omkar)

 3. It works. Switch the scenario from clean morning to festival smog; the next epochs
    mint more, shown per pollutant. (Shreyas)

 4. Remove a plant. Pull one pot; its slot greys out within 10 s and the next epoch mints
    less. (Omkar + Shreyas)

 5. Fake plant. Put the plastic plant with a valid sticker in the slot; it stays dark in NDVI, is
    flagged as suspect and earns nothing. (Omkar + Shreyas)

 6. Reuse a sticker. A second virtual miner submits a proof with one of our sticker IDs; the
    validator rejects it. (Umashankar)

 7. Sell. The owner lists AIRcoin on the marketplace; a buyer account purchases it.
    (Umashankar)

 8. Burn. A factory account buys and burns AIRcoin; its compliance bar fills and a burn
    certificate appears. (Umashankar)

 9. Government view. A citizen submits a miner application; the admin approves it and it
    appears on-chain. The admin dashboard shows all miners on a map, live sensors, mints,
    burns and the rejected sticker from step 6. (Umashankar)
